newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PCIBank sets $500 mln MTN programme.
newsitem.headline: PCIBank sets $500 mln MTN programme.

text.p: The Philippine International Bank (PCIBank) has established a US$500 million global medium term note programme, arranger Merrill Lynch said Monday.
Under the programme, the bank may issue notes and certificates of deposit in an amount outstanding at any time of up to US$500 million, or its equivalent in other currencies.

Currencies may include, without limitation, Australian dollars, Austrian schillings, Canadian dollars, Danish kroner, marks, Dutch guilders, ECU, Finnish markkas, Hong Kong dollars, Irish punts, Italian lire, Japanese yen, New Zealand dollars, South African rand, Swedish kroner, Swiss francs and U.S. dollars, for any maturity subject to regulatory compliance.
Merrill Lynch AG will arrange mark-denominated notes.
The notes may be sold to Qualified Institutional Buyers in the U.S. through Rule 144a or to Institutional Accredited Investors pursuant to Section 4(2) of the U.S. Securities Act.

Dealers on the programme are Merrill Lynch International, ABN AMRO, Credit Lyonnais, DKB, IBJ, J.P. Morgan, SBC Warburg and UBS. Chase Manhattan Bank is the fiscal, issuing and principal paying agent.
Notes issued under the programme will be eligible for listing on the Luxembourg stock exchange.
Clearing will be through Euroclear, Cedel Bank, societe anonyme or any other recognized clearing system.
The Bank is rated Ba3 by Moody's Investors Service.
